video.title: The Easiest Way to Build a Local Newsletter

summary: Chris Koerner builds a local newsletter live for a random US city (Roswell, New Mexico) on Beehive in about 90 minutes. He launches a Meta lead-ad campaign with an instant form, connects it to Beehive via Zapier, and gets his first subscribers within about 10 minutes at roughly $1.15 per lead. He explains monetisation through CPM sponsorships, Beehive boosts and recommendations, referrals, paid tiers and merch, with the claim that a subscriber is worth about 50 cents a month. The key takeaway is to acquire subscribers first with cheap paid ads, then sell sponsorships to local businesses. Beehive is an affiliate partner, so the content is promotional.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office, based in Dallas-Fort Worth, runs several newsletters on Beehive

ideas.name: Local city newsletter (Roswell Dispatch)
ideas.one_liner: Build a free local email newsletter for a mid-sized town, grow subscribers with Meta lead ads, and monetise via CPM sponsorships and other revenue streams.
ideas.business_model: Sponsorship ads sold on a CPM basis, plus Beehive ad network and boosts (pay per new subscriber), affiliate links, paid subscriptions, print-on-demand merch and events.
ideas.customer: Readers: local residents (e.g. ages 25-45) of a town of about 50k+ people. Paying customers: local businesses that sponsor the newsletter.
ideas.problem: Local residents don't know what is happening in their town. Local businesses lack a cheap, targeted way to reach residents.
ideas.offer: A free weekly (or more frequent) email with local news, events, deals and places to visit, with sponsor ads included.

pricing.model: Sponsor ads priced per CPM (per thousand opens); the subscriber side is free, with optional paid tiers.
pricing.notes: Publishing more often multiplies ad revenue because ads are sold per send, but it increases workload.

acquisition_channels.details: Meta (Facebook/Instagram) lead-gen campaign with an instant form asking for email only. Geo-targeted to Roswell, NM, with 'reach more people likely to respond' ticked, placements left open, and a 16-second talking-head phone video with captions. Started at $100/day for one day, then dropped to about $20/day. Got 8 leads in about 10 minutes at about $1.15 per lead.

quote.text: Eight leads, $9. Okay, first of all, I'm going to pause this ad because it's working, right, guys? Okay, $1.15 per meta lead.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Beehive recommendations (newsletter cross-promotion) and boosts (pay-per-subscriber referral from other newsletters, e.g. an Albuquerque newsletter).
Referral widget in the email with rewards such as a bumper sticker, a coupon or a PDF guide. Keep the lowest threshold at one referral.
Publish editions to the Beehive-hosted website so search engines and ChatGPT can index them.

ideas.delivery: Write a weekly email in Beehive using a template (Community Pulse), using ChatGPT for research and copy, and send it to subscribers. Welcome email and surveys are automated. Sponsor ads are sold manually by phone to subscribers who are business owners.
unit_economics_claims: Each subscriber is worth about $0.50 per month at a $50 CPM with a 50% open rate on 5 sends a week
Subscribers stay about 2 years, so the lifetime value is about $12
10,000 subscribers sending 5x a week could earn about $5,000 a month
Acquired first leads at $1.15 each, with a target of 40-50 cents at scale
ideas.startup_cost: About $9 of ad spend for the first leads; Beehive offers a 30-day free trial; a budget of $100 on day one and about $20/day after. Domain and tools otherwise not stated.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: First subscribers within about 90 minutes of starting. No revenue yet; sponsor revenue is not stated and would require building a list and selling sponsors.

acquisition.how: Paid Meta ads plus Zapier sync to Beehive run on their own once set up. Creatives and budgets need occasional human or agent tuning, and ad assets can be generated by AI.

onboarding.how: Welcome email, surveys and Zapier sync of leads into Beehive are fully automated.

delivery.how: Agents can research and draft local news from public sources and send it via Beehive. Human review is needed for accuracy, local credibility and hyperlocal facts.

billing.how: Beehive ad network and boosts pay automatically. Direct local sponsors need invoicing and collection, which is partly automatable.

support.how: Reader replies and sponsor questions are low volume and can be handled by an agent with occasional escalation.

uk_applicability.notes: Works with changes: use a UK town of 50k+, and gather consent properly for UK GDPR/PECR, with a real privacy policy (the video suggests linking a random one, which is not suitable). Meta lead ads and Beehive both operate in the UK. Selling to local sponsors must not use unsolicited emailing of sole traders, but emailing your own subscribers is fine.

risks: Sponsorship revenue is unproven; the video earned none
Lead quality from a low-friction form with no double opt-in may be weak
Meta cost per lead may rise or the initial result may not repeat
Selling sponsors is manual and the CPM assumptions are optimistic for small towns
Platform dependence on Beehive and Meta
Using a random privacy policy would breach UK GDPR

tactics.name: Sell-before-build subscriber acquisition with Meta lead ads
steps: Create a Meta campaign with the Leads objective
Spend $100 on day one so the algorithm learns, then drop to about $20/day
Target the specific town and tick 'reach more people likely to respond'
Use an instant form asking for email only
Make a short 16-second talking-head video with captions and a hook text, and keep the call to action 'find the link below'
Use ChatGPT to write three headlines, texts and descriptions
Create a Facebook Page for the newsletter so the ad doesn't come from a personal brand

quote.text: So, I'm going to put 100, but this is only going to be for a day. Then, I'm going to drop it down to about 20 bucks.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Mine the Meta Ads Library for proven ad formats
steps: Search the Meta Ads Library for 'newsletter'
Filter to active ads in the target country that started before a date a few months back
Filter to the video media type
Treat long-running ads as likely winners and copy their format

tactics.name: Connect Facebook lead ads to Beehive with Zapier
steps: Create a Zap with the Facebook Lead Ads 'New Lead' trigger
Add the Beehive 'Add a subscriber' action using an API key
Set UTM source to 'Facebook ad' and turn on the welcome email
Backfill existing leads
Create a dynamic segment on UTM source to track ad subscribers

tactics.name: Cheap subscriber growth inside Beehive
steps: Use recommendations to swap promotion with other newsletters
Use boosts to pay other newsletters per new subscriber
Add a referral widget with the lowest threshold at one referral
Show a survey right after sign-up to capture data while interest is high

tactics.name: Find sponsors among your own subscribers
steps: Email subscribers asking who wants to advertise
Get responders on the phone
Sell the first ads at $50, $100, $200 and raise the price until people start saying no

quote.text: You get them on the phone and you sell the first out of 50 bucks, 100 bucks, 200 bucks until people start saying no.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Choose a frequency you can sustain
steps: Start with a weekly send
Add more sends only once the routine is stable
Avoid dropping frequency later, as it is demoralising for the publisher

lessons.lesson: Prioritise momentum over perfect setup: skip logos, design and settings until traffic exists.
Work out per-subscriber value and lifetime to set a maximum allowable acquisition cost, then compare ad cost per lead against it.
Hyperlocal niches have tighter targeting, so ad costs per subscriber can be low.
Ask for feedback early and often through polls and surveys at sign-up, when engagement is highest.
Use AI for copy and research, but treat generated output (cities, logos) as drafts that need checking.
Your audience contains your buyers: sponsors can come from your own subscriber list.
Start with a sustainable cadence and add volume later; consistency matters more than ambition.
Compounding growth channels (referrals, recommendations, boosts) reduce dependence on paid ads over time.

evidence_quality.rationale: The ad and Zapier setup is shown live with specific first-hand numbers ($9 for 8 leads), but there is no revenue evidence. All income figures (CPM, $5,000 a month, $12 lifetime value) are hypothetical, and the result is a few minutes of ad data on a fresh page.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Koerner uses a Beehive affiliate link and wants to invest in Beehive. He also promotes his own newsletter (tkopod.com) and a giveaway of the setup.
